Hi Tom / Nina 

Thanks for the questions. Below are practical notes and examples you can hand to your infra team. I also attached a tiny sample repo (integration-sample.zip) and a gist with snippets.

1) SDK & auth
- Node: npm install @redwoodinference/sdk ; Python: pip install redwood-sdk
- Auth options:
  - API key (easy): set env REDWOOD_API_KEY on service; pass via Authorization: Bearer <key>.
  - mTLS (recommended for high-security): configure client cert and use our mTLS endpoint (we'll share example cert setup).

2) Routing & fallback (config example)
- Route by policy: prefer low-latency model variant for requests with header X-RW-Low-Latency: true; fall back to cost-optimized variant when concurrency high.
- Can include route hints in request metadata: { "route_policy": "latency-first" }

3) Structured output / tool calling
- Use our "tools" schema for deterministic actions. Example response envelope: { "tool_call": { "name": "create_ticket", "args": {...} }, "output": "human text" }
- Validate with the SDK's schema validator before invoking downstream systems.

4) Embeddings + reranker flow (recommended)
- Option A (sync rerank): encode candidates -> compute embeddings -> score top-K in-memory -> rerank -> return. Lower tail-latency but higher CPU/latency cost.
- Option B (async): encode candidate set periodically, serve cached candidates; score async then update ranking store. Better cost & throughput.
- Given your 200ms P95 SLO: start with async candidate precomputation + sync embedding of query -> rerank top-100. If you need <200ms P95 for end-to-end, consider an optimized in-memory reranker on smaller K (top-20) and model quantization.

5) Observability hooks (recommended fields & headers)
- Trace header: X-Trace-ID (UUIDv4). We recommend propagating your OpenTelemetry trace id into X-Trace-ID for correlation.
- Latency breakdown header returned by Redwood: X-RW-Latency: model=34ms; infra=12ms; queue=3ms; tokens=120
- Logging fields (log as structured JSON):
  - request_id: <uuid>
  - trace_id: <X-Trace-ID>
  - route: <route_name>
  - model: <model_name>@<version>
  - prompt_hash: <sha256>
  - tokens_generated: <int>
  - latency_ms: <total_ms>
  - latency_breakdown: {"model_ms":.., "infra_ms":.., "queue_ms":..}

Sample middleware (pseudo-code) to ensure header present and log:
- generate trace if missing: X-Trace-ID = uuid.v4()
- attach to outbound request headers
- on response, parse X-RW-Latency and emit structured log with fields above

6) Dashboard recommendations
- Panels: p50/p95/p99 latency (overall), latency breakdown (model vs infra vs queue), errors by route/model, tokens per request distribution, cost per 1M tokens by model.
- Create alert: p95 latency > 200ms for 5m -> page on-call and swap routing to cost-optimized variant.

Attachments: integration-sample.zip (sample code), gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/observability-snippets

Happy to jump on the walkthrough to run through the sample code. If you want, we can include a short live demo of routing failover.
